title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays combined. The overall run time complexity should be O(log(m+n)). Return the result as a string representing a floating point number rounded to 5 decimal places.
constraints: The algorithm must achieve O(log(min(m,n))) time complexity

examples.explanation: The merged array is [1,2,3], and its median is 2.
The merged array is [1,2,3,4], and its median is (2+3)/2 = 2.5.

title: Split Array Largest Sum
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, split nums into k non-empty contiguous subarrays such that the largest sum among these subarrays is minimized. Return the minimized largest sum.
constraints: The subarrays must be contiguous and non-empty

examples.explanation: Splitting into [7,2,5] and [10,8] gives sums 14 and 18. The largest sum is minimized at 18.
Splitting into [1,2,3] and [4,5] gives sums 6 and 9. The largest sum is minimized at 9.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
description: Given an n x n matrix where each row and column is sorted in ascending order, return the kth smallest element in the matrix, using binary search on value range for an efficient solution.

examples.explanation: The sorted order of elements is 1,5,9,10,11,12,13,13,15, and the 8th smallest is 13.
The only element in the matrix is -5, which is the 1st smallest.

title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
description: Given an integer array bloomDay, an integer m, and an integer k, return the minimum number of days needed for us to make m bouquets from the garden. Each bouquet needs k adjacent flowers from the garden, and a flower can only be used once. A flower is available to use on day bloomDay[i] once it has bloomed. If it is impossible to make m bouquets, return -1.

examples.explanation: By day 3, three flowers have bloomed, allowing three bouquets of one flower each to be made.
There aren't enough adjacent blooming flowers to make 3 bouquets of 2 flowers each, so it's impossible.

title: Maximum Number of Removable Characters
description: You are given two strings s and p represented as arrays of characters, where p is a subsequence of s. You are also given an array of distinct integers removable representing indices (0-indexed, into s) that are removed in the order given. Return the maximum k such that after removing the characters at the first k indices from removable, p is still a subsequence of s. Since the strings are given as arrays of characters, s and p are provided as strings, and removable as an array of integers.
constraints: p is a subsequence of s at the start

examples.explanation: After removing the characters at indices 3 and 1, s becomes 'accb' and 'ab' is still a subsequence. Removing index 0 as well breaks it, so the answer is 2.
After removing the character at index 3, 'abcd' is still a subsequence of the resulting string, but removing more breaks it.
